inconsistencies: #36346 and #36778 address the same hazard (transactions arriving during snapshot activation). #36346 is the targeted fix and should be reviewed first; #36778 subsumes it by removing runtime snapshot loading entirely, so a direction call is needed before both are reviewed in depth.

#36598 (demo removal of AssumeUTXO) is in direct tension with #35054, #36778, #36543, #36542, #36500 and #36603, which all extend assumeutxo. The keep-or-remove decision should be settled first; otherwise several P2/P3 reviews may be wasted.

Dependency chain in block-storage/pruning: #36735 -> #36738 -> #36856 -> #36857 (and #36739). #36735 was ranked below its dependents by score; it is raised to P2 and placed first so the chain reads in merge order.
#35861 (Testnet 5) depends on #35793 (BIP 54); only the top commits are new. Review #35793 first.
#36918 is an optimization follow-up to #36895 and is meaningless without it; #36895 first.
#35646 removes M_ERROR from ValidationState and explicitly unblocks #35570; #36792 came out of #35570 review. Review order: #35646, then #36792, then #35570.

#31989 (CTV), #32247 (CSFS) and #29247 (CAT) are all regtest-only / unactivated opcode implementations of comparable consequence and are intended to be composed; they now share a band, with CTV first.

#29491 (Schnorr batch verification) and #32575 (removing the single-threaded script-check path) are coupled: #32575 states it prepares the pipeline for batch validation, so it is the in-tree prerequisite even though #29491 is blocked upstream.
#36735, #36856 and #36857 each claim to fix pruned files left on disk after a failed flush; this work overlaps and should be consolidated rather than reviewed three times.
#35569, #36066 and #35906 all serve the stateless validation library proposal #35904; they should be judged against that plan together, not individually.
#35751 builds on CoinsViewOverlay and #36496 optimizes the same overlay; review #35751 first since #36496 tunes allocations in the path it exercises.
#36149 and #36702 both repair block-index candidate/unlinked-block state on restart; they touch adjacent code and are likely to conflict, so review them back to back.
result.notes: The P2 band is large (26 PRs) because this category genuinely contains many independent storage-error, DoS and performance improvements of comparable weight; within it the ordering puts data-integrity and crash-avoidance first, then measured performance, then proposed-soft-fork and architectural work. P1 is reserved for live crashes, silent corruption, and the consensus-cleanup implementation. Several assumeutxo PRs cluster together and their relative value depends on an unresolved direction question (#36598).
